> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

@pcbeingused333 Thanks for taking Part 1 of #1501. With the built CLI at `f0399d32`, each of the three off switches followed by `pull` removes the recall agent and rule from Claude, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and CodeBuddy. That holds at project and user scope, on the "Already synced" path, and with `--force`. A main build leaves all of them. Turning recall on again writes them back, `doctor` reports nothing missing, and the team's own rule and agent are untouched. tsc, lint and the new unit tests pass, and the new cases fail on main. One thing blocks approval:

- **[P1 blocking] Copies an older release wrote are never removed, and the pull says the member edited them.** A file counts as teamai's only when it equals today's render, so any copy written before the last change to the agent or rule text is kept. Concretely:
  1. With `teamai-cli@0.27.0`: `init` and `pull` with recall on, then the team sets `sharing.recall.enabled: false`, and a 0.27.0 pull leaves the files. That is the bug #1501 describes.
  2. After upgrading to this build, `pull` removes the four rules, but all five agents stay (`.claude`, `.codex` `.toml`, `.cursor`, `.codebuddy`, `.opencode`). The tools keep calling recall.
  3. Every later pull, including "Already synced", warns that they are "not the copy teamai installed". 0.27.0 installed them, and nobody edited them.

  `agents/teamai-recall.md` changed in #1033, so every 0.27.x copy differs. These are exactly the members #1501 is about: they turned recall off on a release that left the files. The body names this limit, but A1 asks for removal "from every enabled tool".

  One way to fix it and keep A2: also count a file as teamai's when it matches what an earlier release shipped, for example a short list of earlier agent and rule bodies (or their digests) rendered per tool, as `LEGACY_RULE_NAMES` and `LEGACY_RECALL_SKILL_NAMES` already do for names. A file teamai can't place could then be named without claiming the member edited it.

  The issue's "the same ownership check `recall disable` uses" doesn't quite exist: `recall disable` removes these files by name (`src/recall-toggle.ts:20-61`). Removing by name here too would drop A2, so that is a call for @jeff-r2026 rather than something to change on your own.

Non-blocking:

- **[P2 non-blocking, but it fits this PR]** Removal looks in fewer places than `recall disable`. It doesn't walk `cleanupOf(...)`, so it misses an agent left in an earlier tool home (#1486). It also checks only each tool's native rule extension, so it misses the `.md` copy older layouts left in a `.mdc` rules folder. Reusing the same location walk as `recall disable` would cover both. We found this in the code and did not run it.
- **[P3 nit]** `warnOnce` deduplicates per process, so a member who keeps an edited copy on purpose sees the warning on every pull.

The CI review found nothing and judged the test record sufficient. We agree on the record. It ran no code, so it couldn't see the older-release case.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

@pcbeingused333 Checked `f3fc1982` with the built CLI next to #1570, which targets the same #1501 item with option (1). Removal by name works on the fast path and on a full sync, at project and user scope. It also removes the copies 0.27.0 (15 files) and 0.28.1 (16) wrote, which #1570 does not. The body now describes option (2), so that point from my last comment is resolved. Two things still block:

- **[P1 blocking] CI is red.** All six Lint & Test jobs fail `pull-agents-cleanup.test.ts`, "never touches built-in or hand-added agents". It fails locally the same way, on this head and on a merge with main. Recall is off by default, so every pull for a team that never turned recall on deletes any file named `teamai-recall.md`, including that test's hand-written one.
- **[P1 blocking] Copies the repository tracks are deleted.** After a pull with recall off, `git status` shows ` D .claude/rules/teamai-recall.md` and ` D .codex/agents/teamai-recall.toml`. Removal passes keep tracked files (`keepsTrackedCopy`, from #915). One `keepsTrackedCopy` check before each removal fixes this, and fixes `recall disable` too.

A note for the member: an edited copy is removed without a line saying so.

@jeff-r2026 The two PRs compared, with the built CLI:

| | #1530, remove by name | #1570, remove unchanged copies only |
|---|---|---|
| Copies from 0.27.0 / 0.28.1 | removed | agents stay and keep calling recall |
| Member-edited copy | removed, silently | kept, silently |
| `teamai recall disable` | unchanged | leaves 8 files from a 0.27.0 install |

I'd land this one once the two points above are fixed, and close #1570.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

@pcbeingused333 Thanks, both blocking points are fixed at `092fcd2e`:

- Removal now skips a copy the repository tracks (`keepsTrackedCopy` before each `remove` in `removeRecallAgentAndRule`), so `recall disable` keeps them too. The new e2e case commits both copies and checks they survive a pull with recall off.
- The unit test now uses a `teamai-other.md` placeholder. Its old `teamai-recall.md` placeholder contradicted the agreed behavior (remove by name), so the change follows the spec rather than weakening the test.

Approving. Optional:
- **[P3 nit]** The "Cost of (2)" note in the body could add that a copy the repository tracks is kept.

CI at `092fcd2e` was green when I approved.

Thanks for implementing (2). I re-reviewed `f3fc1982` with the built CLI, and the code is ready, pending the maintainer's choice between (1) and (2).

**Earlier points:**
- **0.27.x copies:** fixed. After a 0.27.0 install with recall off, the pull removes all 9 recall files (5 agents, 4 rules), at project and user scope, on a full pull and on "Already synced", with no warning.
- **Fewer locations than `recall disable`:** fixed. The pull calls the same function, and an old `.md` copy in Cursor's `.mdc` rules folder is removed.
- **Repeated warning:** gone with the warning.

**What it deletes:**
- **Only these files:** files named `teamai-recall` in teamai's own folders for each tool, and only in a scope where recall resolves off. `teamai-recall-notes.md`, `my-recall.md` and `docs/teamai-recall.md` are kept. A project-scope pull leaves a member's own `~/.claude/agents/teamai-recall.md` alone.
- **Each scope separately:** with `--inherit-user-scope`, each scope keeps its own setting in both directions.
- **For the decision:** one difference from `f0399d32`. Removal now covers every tool, not only the enabled ones: with only Claude and Cursor enabled, the pull also removed `teamai-recall.md` from `.codebuddy/agents`, `.opencode/agents` and `.github/agents`. That's what `recall disable` has always done.

**Still to fix:**
- **[P2 non-blocking, holds approval] The PR body still describes the old behavior.** The Summary, the "New tests" line and the first Notes for Reviewers bullet still say an edited copy is kept and named once. The maintainer will decide from this text, and the squash message comes from it, so please update it to (2).
- **[P3 nit], optional:** nothing is printed when the files are removed, on a normal pull, `--dry-run` or `doctor`, so an edited copy disappears without a line. If (2) stays, one line on a normal pull would tell the member.

**CI review:** its [P1] that edited files are deleted is option (2) by design. That's the open question below, and your comment explains the reasoning. Where it says this contradicts the description, it's right, and that's the body item above.

**Checks:** build, `tsc` and lint pass, and so do the related unit tests (147) and the PR's e2e file. The branch merges cleanly with current main, where `tsc` and the related tests pass too.
